What is the atomic number of Mercury?
Mercury is a chemical element; it has symbol Hg and atomic number 80.
In what year did Josef Mengele die?
Josef Mengele: Before the war, Mengele received doctorates in anthropology and medicine, and he began a career as a researcher.
In what year was Carbon discovered?
Carbon (from Latin carbo 'coal') is a chemical element; it has symbol C and atomic number 6.
Which company manufactures Boeing AH-64 Apache?
Boeing AH-64 Apache: Hughes Helicopters. The Apache began as the Model 77 developed by Hughes Helicopters for the United States Army's Advanced Attack Helicopter program to replace the AH-1 Cobra.
Rendang: Indonesia. It refers to both a cooking method of frying and the dish cooked in that way.
Who is credited with discovering Circinus?
Circinus: Nicolas Louis de Lacaille. Circinus is a small, faint constellation in the southern sky, first defined in 1756 by the French astronomer Nicolas-Louis de Lacaille.
Who is credited with discovering Citric acid?
Citric acid: Carl Wilhelm Scheele. Citric acid is an organic compound with the formula C6H8O7.
Who is credited with discovering Helium?
Helium: Pierre Janssen. Helium (from Ancient Greek: ἥλιος, romanized: helios, lit. 'sun') is a chemical element; it has symbol He and atomic number 2.
Russell Crowe stars in this 2001 Ron Howard film about a Nobel Prize-winning mathematician's struggle with schizophrenia, based on Sylvia Nasar's biography. What's the title?
A Beautiful Mind (film) is a 2001 American biographical drama film about the mathematician John Nash who won a Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences.
Which diverse group of aquatic photosynthetic organisms excludes land plants but includes seaweeds that can grow up to 50 metres long?
Algae (UK also; sing.: alga) are any of a large and diverse group of photosynthetic organisms.

Its name means 'unlike other shrimp.' Known best from the Burgess Shale, this extinct radiodont swam with body flaps and stared out through huge compound eyes packed with lenses — what was this stem-arthropod?

Anomalocaris (from Ancient Greek, meaning "anomalous", and, meaning "shrimp", with the intended meaning "unlike other shrimp") is an extinct genus of radiodont, an order of early-diverging stem-group marine arthropods.
A methyl ester built from aspartic acid and phenylalanine, this non-saccharide sweetener is among the most-studied food additives ever, judged safe by over 100 regulatory bodies — what is it?
Aspartame is an artificial, non-saccharide sweetener commonly used as a sugar substitute in foods and beverages.
Recorded in an ancient Chinese herbal medicine text from around 200 BC and named for a barberry-related plant genus, this yellow-pigmented alkaloid glows under ultraviolet light. What compound is it?
Berberine is an organic compound classified as benzylisoquinoline alkaloid.
Accepted by the American Kennel Club in 1893, this small, compact dog breed with a short tail and erect ears originated in the United States — name the breed?
Boston Terrier is a breed of dog originating in the United States of America.
Its common name is a contraction of 'Mary's gold,' honoring the Virgin Mary, but this daisy-family genus's Latin name nods to the calendar instead — which flowering plant?
Calendula is a genus of about 15-20 species of annual and perennial herbaceous plants in the daisy family, Asteraceae that are often known as marigolds.
This worldwide family of over 5,000 fly species — found everywhere except the Antarctic and Arctic — includes the biting midges also known as sand flies — what is it called?
Ceratopogonidae is a family of flies colloquially known as no-see-ums, sand flies, or biting midges, generally 1-3 millimetres (116-18 in) in length.
This anatomical term for the hollow between a woman's breasts was coined in its modern sense by a Hollywood censor reviewing the 1943 film starring Jane Russell — what is the term?
Cleavage (breasts) is the narrow depression or hollow between the breasts of a woman.
Made up of subregions called the genu, rostrum, trunk, and splenium, this thick nerve tract lets the brain's two hemispheres communicate — what is it?
Corpus callosum (Latin for "tough body"), also callosal commissure, is a wide, thick nerve tract, consisting of a flat bundle of commissural fibers, beneath the cerebral cortex in the brain.
This computer scientist, who died in October 2011, partnered with Ken Thompson to build Unix and also devised the C and B programming languages — who is he?
Covering everything from a fibrous bone condition to a kidney disorder, this term for abnormal tissue growth is usually precancerous rather than outright malignant — what is it?

Dysplasia is any of various types of abnormal growth or development of cells (microscopic scale) or organs (macroscopic scale), and the abnormal histology or anatomical structure(s) resulting from such growth.

This is the only living group of horses, asses, and zebras — odd-toed, herbivorous mammals whose ancestors first evolved in North America before spreading into Asia, Africa, and South America — what is it?
Equus (genus) is a genus of mammals in the perissodactyl family Equidae, which includes horses, asses, and zebras.

First recognised in the 1950s but not formally defined until 1990, this disorder of widespread chronic pain — often with fatigue and memory trouble — has no known cause and is treated multidisciplinarily. What is it?
Fibromyalgia (FM) is a long-term condition characterised by widespread chronic pain.

This inflammation of the stomach lining is commonly caused by H. pylori infection or NSAID use, and can lead to complications like ulcers or, in its autoimmune form, pernicious anemia — what condition is it?
Gastritis is the inflammation of the lining of the stomach. It may occur as a short episode or have a long duration.
Designed in the late 1950s as a replacement for the piston-engined E-1 Tracer, this twin-turboprop U.S. Navy aircraft provides carrier-based early warning radar coverage. Name the aircraft?
Grumman E-2 Hawkeye is an American all-weather, carrier-capable, tactical airborne early warning (AEW) aircraft.

Fox-sized and found on every continent but Australia and Antarctica, these primitive ornithischian dinosaurs are known for odd teeth — canine-like tusks plus cheek teeth built for chewing. What's this family?
Heterodontosauridae is a family of ornithischian dinosaurs that were likely among the most basal (primitive) members of the group.
This birth defect, found in roughly one in every 250 newborn boys, involves an opening that fails to form in its typical location — what condition is this?

Hypospadias is a common malformation in fetal development, most commonly noticed in penises, in which the urethra does not open from its usual location on the head of the penis, or the middle of the vulva.
A pioneer of radio microwave optics who also wrote science fiction and has a lunar crater named for him, this Indian polymath founded Asia's first interdisciplinary research institute — who was he?
Jagadish Chandra Bose (30 November 1858 - 23 November 1937) was an Indian polymath with interests in biology, physics and writing science fiction.
Honored across Asia as a model healer and "Medicine King," this 5th-century BCE physician of Rajgir tended to King Bimbisāra — and to the Buddha himself. Who was he?
Jīvaka was the personal physician of the Buddha and the Indian King Bimbisra.
Closely related to earthworms but equipped with a sucker at each end, these segmented parasitic or predatory worms make up their own subclass within the annelid phylum — what are they?
Leech are segmented parasitic or predatory worms that comprise the subclass Hirudinea within the phylum Annelida.

Ranging across Eurasia with plumage of black, white, pink, and grey, this small insectivorous bird forms compact family flocks of six to seventeen outside the breeding season, its northern subspecies sporting all-white heads — which bird?
Long-tailed tit (Aegithalos caudatus) is a common bird species belonging to the bushtit family found throughout Eurasia.

Dubbed "sea locusts" by the ancient Assyrians and "prawn killers" elsewhere, these burrow-dwelling marine crustaceans are among the top predators of tropical shallows — yet they remain poorly understood. What are they?
Mantis shrimp are carnivorous marine crustaceans of the order Stomatopoda (from Ancient Greek (stma) 'mouth' and (pos) 'foot').
This field's founding body, the Bureau International des Poids et Mesures, grew out of an 1875 convention and eventually gave the world the International System of Units — what is this study called?
Metrology is the scientific study of measurement.
An Austrian-School economist who called the state 'robbery systematized and writ large,' he founded and championed anarcho-capitalism across more than twenty books — who was he?
Murray Rothbard (March 2, 1926 - January 7, 1995) was an American economist of the Austrian School, economic historian, political theorist, and activist.

First described in 1766 by naturalist Peter Simon Pallas, this sole living member of its genus sports a white throat patch and, in males only, a pair of short horns — what is this large Asian antelope called?
Nilgai (Boselaphus tragocamelus) (literally meaning "blue cow") is the largest antelope in Asia.
Found on every continent except Antarctica, this fish-eating raptor nests near water and can be identified by its brown back and pale, grayish head — what bird is it?
Osprey (Pandion haliaetus), historically known as sea hawk, river hawk, and fish hawk, is a diurnal, fish-eating bird of prey with a cosmopolitan range.
Innervated by two dedicated nerves and inserting near the upper arm's bicipital groove, which broad chest muscle flexes and internally rotates the humerus?
Pectoralis major (from Latin pectus 'breast') is a thick, fan-shaped or triangular convergent muscle of the human chest.
This French physicist shared the 1903 Nobel Prize in Physics with his wife, making them the first married couple ever to win a Nobel — who is he?
Pierre Curie (15 May 1859 - 19 April 1906) was a French physicist and chemist, and a pioneer in crystallography and magnetism.
Used to disinfect both healthcare workers' hands and patients' skin before and after surgery, this antiseptic can be applied as a liquid, ointment, or powder — which compound?

Povidone-iodine is an antiseptic used for skin disinfection before and after surgery. Povidone-iodine (PVP-I), also known as iodopovidone, is an antiseptic used for skin disinfection before and after surgery.
The sole member of the genus Setonix, this cat-sized, mainly nocturnal Australian marsupial famously inhabits Rottnest Island — what is it?
Quokka (Setonix brachyurus) is a small macropod about the size of a domestic cat.

This English mathematical physicist shared a 1988 Wolf Prize with Stephen Hawking, won a 2020 Nobel for black-hole work, and dreamed up an 'impossible' triangle that inspired M. C. Escher — who is he?
Roger Penrose (born 8 August 1931) is an English mathematician, mathematical physicist, and philosopher of science.
Developed by the MIT Media Lab for children ages 5 to 16, this block-based visual programming language and website has been translated into more than 70 languages — name it?
Scratch (programming language) is a high-level, block-based visual programming language and website aimed primarily at children as an educational tool, with a target audience of ages 5 to 16.
This group of nocturnal Southeast Asian primates ranges from Yunnan province in China down to the island of Java, with a pygmy relative recently reclassified into its own genus — what are they?
Slow loris are a group of several species of nocturnal strepsirrhine primates that make up the genus Nycticebus.
Built from four fused rings, compounds in this class include cholesterol, testosterone, and anti-inflammatory drugs like dexamethasone. What class of compound is it?
Steroid is an organic compound with four fused rings (designated A, B, C, and D) arranged in a specific molecular configuration.
Symbol Tc, atomic number 43: this silvery-gray metal is entirely synthetic, though tiny natural traces form via neutron capture in molybdenum ore — what element?
Technetium is a chemical element; it has symbol Tc and atomic number 43.
This metric unit of mass equals exactly 1,000 kilograms — about 2,204.6 pounds — and is technically identical to the SI unit called the megagram. What is it?
Tonne (or; symbol: t) is a unit of mass equal to 1,000 kilograms.

First identified in 1801 by a Spanish-Mexican scientist analyzing a mineral he dubbed 'brown lead,' this hard, silvery-grey transition metal carries atomic number 23 and chemical symbol V — what's the element?
Vanadium is a chemical element; it has symbol V and atomic number 23.
The largest land-dwelling member of the weasel family, this solitary, muscular carnivore of the northern boreal forests can kill prey far larger than itself — what animal is it?
Wolverine (US also; Gulo gulo), also called the carcajou or quickhatch (from East Cree, kwiihkwahaacheew), is the largest land-dwelling member of the family Mustelidae.
Accidentally discovered in 1967 by German chemist Karl Clauss at Hoechst AG, which calorie-free artificial sweetener is sold under the brand names Sunett and Sweet One?

Designed to replace the Lockheed C-130 Hercules and sized between it and the Boeing C-17, this four-engine European turboprop military transporter first flew from Seville in December 2009 despite nearly being cancelled over cost overruns. What's the aircraft?
Airbus A400M Atlas: Multi-national four-engine turboprop military transport aircraft.
A striking red-capped, white-warted mushroom of northern forests, this fungus may owe its name to an old use against flies — or to a medieval belief that flies caused madness. What is it?
Amanita muscaria: Species of mushroom. Amanita muscaria, commonly known as the fly agaric or fly amanita, is a basidiomycete fungus of the genus Amanita.

Multicellular eukaryotes that breathe oxygen and grow from a hollow ball of cells called a blastula, over 1.5 million species in this kingdom have been described by scientists. What are they collectively called?
Animal: Biological kingdom. Over 1.5 million living animal species have been described, of which around 1.05 million are insects, over 85,000 are molluscs, and around 65,000 are vertebrates.
The clinging seed burrs of this plant genus, commonly known as burdock, directly inspired the invention of the hook-and-loop fastener — which genus?

Also called the moon jellyfish, this once-thought-cosmopolitan species was split into roughly 28 separate species in the 2020s and is now known to live only in the north Atlantic and off Argentina — which species?
Aurelia aurita: Species of jellyfish. The species now identified as A. aurita is only found in the north Atlantic and in Argentina, and is not dangerous to humans.
Making up nearly 40% of all known insects with around 400,000 described species, this order is distinguished by front wings hardened into protective cases called elytra — what creatures are these?
Beetle: Order of insects. Over 300 species are used as food, mostly as larvae; species widely consumed include mealworms and rhinoceros beetle larvae.

Despite its name, this African animal's hide actually ranges from brown to grey, and it's distinguished from its 'white' cousin by a pointed, hooked upper lip rather than a wide, square one — which species?
Black rhinoceros: Species of mammal. Although the species is referred to as black, its colours vary from brown to grey.
Nicknamed 'murderer's thumb' or 'stubbed thumb,' this genetic trait gives about 2% of people a short, rounded thumb linked to the HOXD13 gene — what is it?
Brachydactyly type D: Abnormal shortening of the distal part of the thumb.
Alongside HTML and JavaScript, which style sheet language handles the layout, colors, and fonts of a webpage — separating presentation from content?
CSS: Style sheet language. CSS is a cornerstone technology of the World Wide Web, alongside HTML and JavaScript.

Time called her the "literary godmother" to Paris's Lost Generation, and her Black Sun Press printed early Hemingway and Henry Miller — but she also patented the first successful modern bra. Who was she?
Usually arising from damage to the developing brain before birth, this group of childhood movement disorders causes stiff or weak muscles, tremors, and poor coordination — what condition?
Cerebral palsy: Movement disorders that appear in early childhood.
Every animal in this group shares five telltale traits — including a notochord, pharyngeal slits, and a tail that extends past the anus — at some stage of life; which of these belongs to that phylum?
Chordate: Phylum of animals having a dorsal nerve cord.
This genus of demersal fish, named by Linnaeus in 1758, includes an Atlantic and a Pacific species prized for their mild flavor and flaky white flesh — what fish is it?
Cod: Common name for several fish, but mainly the demersal genus Gadus.
Caused by a fungus that forms galls on maize plants, this disease produces an edible delicacy in Mexico known as huitlacoche, often stuffed into quesadillas — which condition?
Corn smut: Fungal plant disease on maize and teosinte.
Also called Bermuda grass, this hardy warm-climate turf species is ironically not native to the island of the same name — which plant, by its scientific name?
Cynodon dactylon: Species of grass. Cynodon dactylon, commonly known as Bermuda grass or as couch grass in Australia and New Zealand, is a grass found worldwide in warm and tropical climates.
This central nervous system stimulant is the 'right-handed' mirror-image form of a well-known molecule, prescribed for ADHD and narcolepsy and sometimes given as an inactive prodrug — what is it?
Dextroamphetamine: CNS stimulant and isomer of amphetamine.
A broad-spectrum member of the tetracycline class, this antibiotic treats everything from acne and chlamydia to Lyme disease and cholera — though it'll make you sunburn more easily. Which drug?
Doxycycline: Tetracycline-class antibiotic. It is used to treat bacterial pneumonia, acne, chlamydia infections, Lyme disease, cholera, typhus, and syphilis, and is sometimes used to prevent malaria.
Despite its name, this South American freshwater fish is actually a knifefish, not a true eel, and produces powerful discharges using specialized tissue — which species?
Electrophorus electricus: South American electric fish. It is considered as a freshwater teleost which contains an electrogenic tissue that produces electric discharges.
This flowering shrub in the family Erythroxylaceae is one of only two species whose leaves are cultivated to produce a notorious stimulant — which plant is it?
Erythroxylum coca: Species of flowering plant.
Sporting an orange-red breast rimmed in grey and brown upperparts, this small insect-eating songbird ranges from Western Siberia to North Africa — which bird?
European robin: Species of bird. It is found across Europe, as far east as Western Siberia, and as far south as North Africa.

Boldly patterned in black and yellow to warn predators of its toxicity, this European amphibian can live for more than 50 years and is now vulnerable due to an introduced fungal disease — what species is it?
Fire salamander: Species of amphibian. The fire salamander (Salamandra salamandra) is a common species of salamander found in Europe.
Traditionally pounded from cassava, plantains, and cocoyam, this West African staple gets a shoutout in Chinua Achebe's novel Things Fall Apart — what dish is it?
Fufu: Dough-like food in African cuisine.
The largest of its family, this mostly solitary mammal uses long foreclaws to dig into nests and a sticky tongue to slurp up ants and termites — what animal is it?
Giant anteater: Species of mammal. The giant anteater (Myrmecophaga tridactyla) is an insectivorous mammal native to Central and South America.
One of China's 'Four Great Domestic Fish,' this herbivorous freshwater species was later introduced to Europe and the US to control aquatic weeds — which fish?
Grass carp: Species of fish. This Asian carp is the only species of the genus Ctenopharyngodon.
This British mathematician has studied the math of dating and pandemics, delivered the Royal Institution's 2019 Christmas Lectures, and hosted BBC's 'Secret Genius of Modern Life' — who is she?
Hannah Fry: British mathematician and broadcaster (born 1984)
Found in trace amounts in modern gasoline blends, this colorless, six-carbon alkane boils at about 69°C and serves as a cheap, low-reactivity solvent — what is it?
A colorless gas that throws off white fumes the moment it meets moist air, it turns into a familiar strong acid once dissolved in water — which compound, formula HCl?
Hydrogen chloride: Chemical compound. Hydrogen chloride gas and hydrochloric acid are important in technology and industry.

Also known as the spectacled or binocellate snake, this reptile from South Asia is one of the 'Big Four' species responsible for most snakebites in the region and is revered in Hindu mythology — which snake?
Indian cobra: Species of snake. The species is native to the Indian subcontinent, and is a member of the "Big Four" species that are responsible for the most snakebite cases in Sri Lanka and India.
Awarded a gas-attack Iron Cross in WWI before sharing the 1925 Nobel with Gustav Hertz for the laws of how an electron strikes an atom — who was this German-American physicist?
Hailed as a 'miracle worker' in 1955, this researcher refused to patent his polio vaccine so it could spread worldwide for free — who is he?
Jonas Salk: American inventor of the polio vaccine (1914–1995)

Also called 47,XXY, this chromosome anomaly leaves those affected phenotypically male but often infertile, and is named after the American endocrinologist who first identified it in the 1940s — what's the condition?
Called a 'universal genius,' this Swiss polymath founded graph theory and topology while introducing much of modern mathematical notation — who is he?

Developed under the US Air Force's Advanced Tactical Fighter program, this American twin-engine stealth fighter was designed for air superiority but also handles ground attack, electronic warfare and signals intelligence — which aircraft?

Lockheed Martin F-22 Raptor: American stealth air superiority fighter. The Lockheed Martin–Boeing F-22 Raptor is an American twin-engine, jet-powered, all-weather, supersonic stealth fighter aircraft.
This is the common name for the larva of flies like houseflies and blowflies — though, confusingly, not for baby mosquitoes — what is it called?
Growing out of calculus and the study of derivatives and integrals, this branch of mathematics examines functions, spaces, and limits using methods of approximation and convergence — which field?

Mathematical analysis: Branch of mathematics. Mathematical analysis is the branch of mathematics that studies functions, spaces, and operators through quantitative methods of approximation and convergence.
Sold under the brand Glucophage, this first-line oral medication for type 2 diabetes is favored partly because it isn't associated with weight gain. What drug is it?
Metformin: Medication used to treat diabetes.
Medically termed a 'spontaneous abortion,' this is the loss of an embryo or fetus before it can survive independently — distinct from a stillbirth, which occurs after 20 weeks. What is it?
Miscarriage: Natural premature termination of pregnancy.
This Austrian-School economist founded anarcho-capitalism and called the state "the organization of robbery systematized and writ large" — which libertarian theoretician?
The sole species in its genus and a fixture of Mediterranean gardens, this drought-and-flood-tolerant shrub of the dogbane family is also called rose laurel or rosebay — what is it?
Nerium: Species of plant. It is the only species currently classified in the genus Nerium, belonging to subfamily Apocynoideae of the dogbane family Apocynaceae.
Represented by symbols like '11' in the Hindu-Arabic system used worldwide, these mathematical objects serve to count, measure, and label — what are they called?
Number: Used to count, measure, and label. The most basic examples are the natural numbers: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and so forth.
Described as far back as the 300s BC by Hippocrates, this bone infection most often strikes the spine in adults and the long bones in children — which condition?
Osteomyelitis: Infection of the bones. It may be acute or chronic and can be classified as hematogenous or non-hematogenous.
Also known as trisomy 13, this chromosomal condition arises when cells carry extra genetic material from chromosome 13, causing widespread organ defects — which syndrome?
Patau syndrome: Chromosomal disorder in which there are three copies of chromosome 13.
This legume's raw seeds contain a toxic compound that must be boiled away before eating, though its unripe green pods are eaten as-is — which species is it?

Derived in 1900 by a German physicist who proposed that an oscillator's energy could only change in discrete increments, this principle describes the spectral density of radiation from a black body at a given temperature — what is it called?
Planck's law: Spectral density of light emitted by a black body.
This common name describes small aquatic crustaceans with an exoskeleton and ten legs, especially popular in the UK and Commonwealth nations for larger swimming decapods — what is it?
Prawn: Common name applied to some types of crustaceans.
Ranging from Penguin Random House to countless small independent players, which broad industry covers making books, magazines, music, and software available to the public, in print or digital form?
Publishing: Production and distribution of media.

In a late stage of stellar evolution, this puffed-up, low-to-intermediate-mass star has a surface temperature around 5,000 K and burns helium or hydrogen in shells around its core — what type of star is it?
Red giant: Type of large cool star.
Also called a dassie, this small African and Middle Eastern mammal lives in crevice colonies of up to 80 and posts lookouts to warn of approaching predators — which animal?
Rock hyrax: Species of mammal native to Africa and the Middle East.
Dropped out of Stanford to co-found Loopt, later led Y Combinator, then became CEO of the company behind ChatGPT — briefly ousted by its board in 2023 for not being 'consistently candid.' Who is he?
Sam Altman: American entrepreneur and investor (born 1985)
Encompassing several superfamilies and families, this taxonomic order groups together cephalopods that each have ten arms — which order is it?
Found from Bangladesh to the Philippines, these nocturnal primates make up the genus Nycticebus and include at least eight recognized species — what are they called?
Slow loris: Genus of primates from Southeast Asia.
The sole living member of its genus, this slender, long-legged antelope of southwest Africa sports a white face, a dark eye-to-mouth stripe, and backward-curving horns on both sexes — what is it?
Springbok: Antelope of southwest and south Africa. The springbok or springbuck (Antidorcas marsupialis) is an antelope found mainly in south and southwest Africa.
Described as the most economically important oxide of its element, this compound with the formula SO3 is a key precursor to sulfuric acid and to acid rain — what is it?
Sulfur trioxide: Chemical compound. Sulfur trioxide exists in several forms: gaseous monomer, crystalline trimer, and solid polymer.
Which calculus result approximates a differentiable function near a point using a polynomial — its first-order version being the familiar linear approximation?

Taylor's theorem: Approximation of a function by a polynomial. There are several versions of Taylor's theorem, some giving explicit estimates of the approximation error of the function by its Taylor polynomial.
Commonly nicknamed 'tree of life' from Latin, this genus of coniferous evergreens in the cypress family includes species native to both North America and eastern Asia. What's the genus?
Thuja: Genus of conifers. Thuja ( THEW-yə) is a genus of coniferous tree or shrub in the Cupressaceae (cypress family).
Which mathematical principle states that, for any three-sided shape, the sum of two side lengths must be at least as long as the third?
Triangle inequality: Property of geometry, also used to generalize the notion of "distance" in metric spaces.
This hormone-responsive organ nourishes a developing embryo and fetus until birth, connecting at its narrow lower end to the cervix and at its upper corners to the fallopian tubes — what is it?
Uterus: Female sex organ in mammals.
Usually appearing on the hands and feet due to a human papillomavirus infection, this benign skin growth typically clears on its own within months to years — what is this common growth called?
Wart: Small, rough growth resembling a cauliflower or a solid blister.
One of Europe's largest bee species, this dark, iridescent carpenter bee nests in dead wood and is generally not aggressive unless provoked — which insect?
Xylocopa violacea: Species of bee. Xylocopa violacea, the violet carpenter bee, is the common European species of carpenter bee, and one of the largest bees in Europe.

What is the chemical symbol for krypton?
The symbol for krypton is Kr. Krypton is a chemical element; it has symbol Kr and atomic number 36.

Ethan Hawke: Ethan Green Hawke (born November 6, 1970) is an American actor, author, and filmmaker whose career on both stage and screen has spanned four decades.

Carrie Fisher: Carrie Frances Fisher (October 21, 1956 – December 27, 2016) was an American actress and writer.
